newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-French insurer Axa's profits jump pre-merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French insurer Axa's profits jump pre-merger.

text.p: Axa, which is merging with rival French insurer UAP to create the world's second largest insurer, posted a 39.5 percent rise in 1996 profit to 3.81 billion francs ($670.4 million) on Wednesday.

As it cleared the decks for the megamerger, UAP announced a loss of 6.45 billion francs after writing off 7.59 billion francs in one-off charges to purge its books and prevent money-losing activities weighing on the new group's future.

Stripping out the one-off charges -- which included cover for businesses in a collapsed property sector as well as the deconsolidation of French bank BNP in its accounts -- UAP' said its profit was 1.14 billion francs.

Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris are teaming up to form Axa-UAP this year after springing the news on financial markets in November that they would combine their operations to create a French heavyweight in the global insurance business.
Wednesday was the last time that Axa and UAP, France's two biggest insurers, will produce two separate sets of figures. As of this year their accounts will be consolidated.

Axa, widely regarded as a thrusting French insurer and the driving force of the new duo, said in a results statement it was aiming for average growth of 15 percent a year in net profit per share between 1996 and the year 2000.

It also said it was seeking return on equity, a key measure of performance in the industry, of 15 percent in the medium term and of 11 percent in 1998. That is after reporting return on equity of 10.2 percent in 1996 and 8.5 percent in 1995.
Axa said its 1996 performance was driven by life insurance results, due to a strong improvement in the United States, France and Britain.

Axa's performance was also lifted by property and casualty insurance results which increased strongly in France, Belgium and Britain. The exception was Axa Global Risks in Britain, which posted losses due to the strengthening of reserves related to claims prior to 1992.
First time full year consolidation of National Mutual in Australia, consolidated for one month only in 1995, helped boost profits, the firm said.

There was a hefty increase in net income from U.S. financial services -- DLJ and Alliance Capital Management -- and a strong contribution from the holding company thanks to "very good investment results."
Changes in local accounting methods in life insuarance at Dutch and Canadian subisidiaries added extraordinary profits, while favourable currency fluctuations also helped, it said.
But some downward pressure on profits came from losses at the Axa Leben life insurance unit in Germany and at French real estate subsidiaries due to real estate valuation allowances.
